quizName: DMV Practice Test #3 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: The front brake is:

options.text: Only for use if the rear brake fails.

questions.explanation: The front brake is safe when used correctly. The front brake provides most of the stopping power—about three-fourths of the total.

questions.question: The shortest and safest stops happen by:

options.text: Letting the front tire lock up.
Using both the front and rear brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes together in a smooth, gradual way to stop shortest and safest. Do not lock up either tire.

questions.question: For motorcycle safety, you should:

options.text: Check your motorcycle before every ride.
Check your motorcycle once a month.
Check your motorcycle twice a week.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your motorcycle before every ride.
questions.explanation: Small problems on a motorcycle are more serious than on a car. Check your motorcycle thoroughly before every ride.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle:

options.text: It is good to drag your feet.
Keep your feet firmly on the footrests.
Keep your feet away from the controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Put your feet firmly on the footrests for good balance. Do not drag them on the ground. Do not point your toes down, as they may catch on the road. Keep your feet near the controls so you can reach them quickly.

questions.question: Reflective clothing should be worn:
questions.explanation: Bright and reflective clothing helps other drivers see you in any condition. Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight, so wear bright clothing all day and all night.

questions.question: What should you check before every ride?
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tires, oil, fluids, lights, signals, brake light, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: Which color helps you be seen while riding?
questions.explanation: Orange, red, yellow, and green are good colors to wear. Wear bright colors any time of day.

questions.question: Keep a safe distance behind other vehicles to:

options.text: Give yourself time and space to see and react to hazards.
Help traffic counters count you as a vehicle.
Encourage other drivers to cut you off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give yourself time and space to see and react to hazards.
questions.explanation: A safe following distance gives you space to stop or swerve if the vehicle ahead stops suddenly. It also helps you see road hazards like potholes.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, you should:

options.text: Prepare and adjust your motorcycle for the passenger.
Ride the same way as without a passenger.
Tell the passenger what to do after you start riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prepare and adjust your motorcycle for the passenger.
questions.explanation: Only carry a passenger if your motorcycle is equipped for it. Your motorcycle needs passenger footrests and a large enough seat. You may need to adjust the headlight, tire pressure, and suspension for the extra weight.

questions.question: A three-wheeled motorcycle:

options.text: Handles curves the same as a two-wheeled motorcycle.
Handles curves differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.
Should not be ridden in curves.
Should use the shoulder when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Handles curves differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Three-wheeled motorcycles and motorcycles with sidecars turn differently than two-wheeled motorcycles.

questions.question: If you wait one hour after drinking one drink before riding:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
It is fine as long as you ride slowly.
Alcohol may still be in your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol may still be in your body.
questions.explanation: Your body removes about one drink per hour on average. The time needed varies from person to person. The safest choice is not to ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: If you wait one hour per drink before riding your motorcycle:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your skills will not be affected.
You will be fine as long as you ride slowly.

questions.explanation: Your body removes about one drink per hour on average. Alcohol can build up in your system even if you drink slowly. This buildup can still affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: A benefit of regular motorcycle maintenance is that:

options.text: Your motorcycle will run well for a long time.
Maintenance checks take a lot of time.
Maintenance checks help prevent parking tickets.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle will run well for a long time.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle will ride like new if you maintain it properly. Regular maintenance checks are an important part of motorcycle upkeep.

questions.question: How do you control the accelerator on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The accelerator is on the right handgrip. You control it with your right hand.

questions.question: A motorcyclist should:

options.text: Stay in the same part of the lane all the time.
Move back and forth across the lane to keep other drivers out.
Change lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
Not worry about where they are in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position all the time. Move your position in the lane based on changes in road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: Intersections are usually:

options.text: Safe because there is lots of traffic.

questions.explanation: Intersections are dangerous because many things can go wrong when motorcyclists and other drivers meet there.

questions.question: In normal conditions, keep a minimum following distance of:
questions.explanation: In normal conditions, stay at least two seconds behind the vehicle ahead of you. Increase this distance if conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: To help other drivers see you, wear:
questions.explanation: Bright-colored clothing helps other drivers see you. Wear colors that stand out during the day and at night.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should wear a jacket:

options.text: Only on rides longer than half an hour.

questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket when riding, even in warm weather. It protects you from sun damage and helps prevent dehydration.

questions.question: What does a face shield do?

options.text: Does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic face shield gives the best protection for your eyes and face. Regular glasses are not enough. In Vermont, you do not have to wear eye protection if your motorcycle has a windshield, but it is still a good idea.

questions.question: Can you pass another vehicle in a no passing zone?

options.text: Yes, a motorcycle can still pass.
Yes, if you can finish before another vehicle comes.
Yes, you can pass on the shoulder.

questions.explanation: Passing is not allowed in no passing zones. You also cannot pass by riding off the road.

questions.question: Why should motorcycle riders turn their heads to look over their shoulders before changing lanes?

options.text: Motorcycles have blind spots like other vehicles.
It helps you make eye contact with other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots like other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots that mirrors cannot show. Always turn your head to check for vehicles or hazards in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle rider improve their visibility?
questions.explanation: To be seen better, wear bright clothes with reflective material. Use your headlight at all times. Use your signals and brake light correctly.

questions.question: What happens when you take a corner too fast?

options.text: You may cross into another lane.
It is better than going too slowly.
You will usually stay in your lane.
It is okay because motorcycles are small.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may cross into another lane.
questions.explanation: Taking a corner too fast can cause you to cross into another lane or go off the road. Slow down before you start to turn.
